prompt: Which elements make up the main group elements?

choices.text: The elements of the s and p blocks of the periodic table
The elements of the d block
choices.why: The d block holds the transition metals. The main group elements are the s- and p-block elements.

choices.text: Only the nonmetals
choices.why: The main group includes metals such as sodium and aluminum as well as nonmetals: it is the whole s and p blocks.

choices.text: Only the noble gases and the halogens
choices.why: Those are just two groups of the p block. The main group is every element in the s and p blocks.

explanation: The main group elements are those in the s and p blocks of the periodic table.

prompt: What does the list of the top 25 industrial chemicals produced in the US in 2002 show about the main group elements?

choices.text: Thirteen of the 25 are inorganic main group compounds, so these elements are of tremendous societal importance
None of the 25 contain main group elements
choices.why: Thirteen of the top 25 are inorganic main group compounds.

choices.text: Only transition metal compounds are made on an industrial scale
choices.why: Over half of the top 25 chemicals are inorganic main group compounds.

choices.text: Main group compounds matter only as curiosities, with no industrial use
choices.why: The section stresses the opposite: main group compounds make up 13 of the top 25 chemicals produced.

explanation: Besides being fundamental constituents of ordinary matter with a rich chemistry, the main group elements are of tremendous societal importance: thirteen of the top 25 chemicals produced in the United States are inorganic main group compounds.

prompt: What is meant by "descriptive chemistry" in this chapter?

choices.text: Presenting information about the chemistry of the elements, as opposed to fundamental concepts, theories, and models
Deriving the theories of bonding from first principles
choices.why: That is the conceptual side of chemistry. Descriptive chemistry presents what the elements and their compounds actually do.

choices.text: An exhaustive catalogue of every known compound of each element
choices.why: The chapter says no attempt will be made to be exhaustive; it focuses on important or characteristic features.

choices.text: Describing only the physical appearance of the elements
choices.why: Descriptive chemistry covers the chemistry of the elements (their reactions, compounds and properties), not just their appearance.

explanation: In general, descriptive chemistry presents information about the chemistry of the elements, as opposed to describing more fundamental concepts, theories, and models. The chapter focuses on important or characteristic features rather than trying to be exhaustive.

prompt: The aluminum chloride dimer and pentaborane(9) are shown at the start of the chapter. What point do they illustrate?

choices.text: The bonds holding main group compounds together do not always obey the rules taught in general and organic chemistry
All main group compounds can be described with ordinary two-center, two-electron bonds
choices.why: These examples were chosen because they can't: they contain bridging and cluster bonds.

choices.text: Main group elements form only ionic compounds
choices.why: Both examples are held together by covalent bridge and cluster bonds, not simple ionic bonding.

choices.text: Aluminum and boron never form compounds with more than one metal or boron atom
choices.why: The aluminum chloride dimer has two Al centers and pentaborane has a cluster of five B atoms.

explanation: In the aluminum chloride dimer, chlorine atoms bridge the Al centers, and pentaborane nonahydride contains B–H–B bridge bonds and cluster bonds. These structures show that main group bonding does not always follow the rules of typical general and organic chemistry courses, and the chapter uses such cases to enlarge the range of structures you consider possible.

prompt: How are the two aluminum centers held together in the aluminum chloride dimer?

choices.text: Chlorine atoms bridge the two Al centers
A direct Al–Al bond
choices.why: In the dimer the two Al atoms are linked through bridging chlorine atoms, not an Al–Al bond.

choices.text: Bridging hydrogen atoms
choices.why: There is no hydrogen in aluminum chloride; B–H–B bridges are the feature of pentaborane, not of the Al2Cl6 dimer.

choices.text: Purely ionic attraction between Al^3+ and Cl^− ions in a lattice
choices.why: The dimer is a discrete molecule in which chlorine atoms bridge the Al centers.

explanation: In the aluminum chloride dimer, chlorine atoms bridge the Al centers, an arrangement that is not covered by the simple bonding rules of introductory courses.

prompt: Pentaborane nonahydride has a cluster of five B atoms held together by cluster bonds. How many B–H–B bridge bonds are arranged around the open face of the cluster?
explanation: The structure of pentaborane nonahydride includes four B–H–B bridge bonds arranged around the open face of a cluster of five B atoms held together by cluster bonds.
